messages.text: ok I need a study plan. I'm sitting the IPC exam (Interior Practice Certification) sometime in August, haven't got the exact date yet. it's three papers: codes & compliance, professional practice, and a design brief under time pressure

That's a good amount of runway: roughly 14 weeks. I'd split it into three phases: foundations (weeks 1-5), practice papers (weeks 6-11) and timed mocks plus review (weeks 12-14). Codes and compliance usually needs the most repetition, so give it a little more weight early. How many hours a week can you realistically give it?
maybe 10? I do 6 to 8 every weekday morning at the State Library before work, that's my best brain time

Ten hours a week works. Two hours each weekday morning gives you exactly that, which leaves weekends free for rest or an occasional mock. I'd keep Fridays lighter, for review rather than new material.
sounds good. what's the best way to memorise the building classes and egress rules? they all blur together

Most people find it easier to anchor rules to real buildings. Pick one example building for each class and annotate a floor plan with the egress distances and fire separation it needs. Spaced repetition flashcards also help for the raw numbers.
honestly flashcards don't work for me at all, I learn by drawing. if I sketch it I remember it

Then lean into that. Make a sketchbook just for the exam: one page per building class with a quick plan, the exits, travel distances and required ratings written onto the drawing. Redraw each page from memory a week later and compare.
love that. ok and the timed design brief - in practice it's 3 hours for a full concept. at work at Halcyon & Reed I'd get two weeks for that lol

The timed brief rewards a fixed routine more than talent. Spend 20 minutes reading and listing constraints, 30 minutes on zoning diagrams, 90 on the main plan and two key views, and keep 40 for notes and checking. Practise that sequence until it's automatic.
ok that's actually helpful. would joining a study group be worth it?

It can be, especially for professional practice questions where discussing scenarios helps. You might look for an IPC study group in Melbourne that meets weekly, or start one with a couple of colleagues.
nah I don't think so, I'm better alone and my evenings are already chaos. can you put the 14 weeks into a table?

Here's the outline: Weeks 1-5 codes and compliance foundations with the sketchbook method, plus one professional practice chapter a week. Weeks 6-11 one past paper section every Friday and weak-topic redraws. Weeks 12-14 two full timed mocks on Saturdays and light review on weekdays. I can expand any week into daily tasks.

messages.text: how do i integrate x*e^x again, i always forget which bit is u

Use integration by parts with u = x and dv = e^x dx. Then du = dx and v = e^x, so the integral is x e^x minus the integral of e^x, which gives x e^x - e^x + C. The LIATE rule helps: pick the algebraic term as u before the exponential.
ohh LIATE. ok and x^2 e^x is just doing it twice?
Exactly. First pass with u = x^2 gives x^2 e^x minus 2 times the integral of x e^x, and you already know that one. Final answer: e^x (x^2 - 2x + 2) + C.
